previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of mesenteric fibromatosis, chronic abdominal pain, and TPN dependence was admitted directly from GI clinic due to severe, uncontrolled pain and malnutrition after discontinuing home TPN for three weeks. She was restarted on hospital TPN with improved tolerance and nutritional support. Pain management was optimized through consultation with the chronic pain service, including a trial of Dilaudid PCA, followed by multiple medication adjustments, ultimately transitioning to methadone. A new left thigh hematoma was identified, associated with supratherapeutic anticoagulation from home Lovenox; it was managed conservatively with dose reduction to prophylactic levels, warm/cold compresses, and a lidocaine patch. Her nausea improved, anemia was monitored, and she remained stable without active bleeding or infection. She was discharged home with services on adjusted pain and anticoagulation regimens, new TPN formula, and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with complex medical history including 
mesenteric fibromatosis requiring multiple abdominal surgeries 
for SBO/pain, s/p venting g-tube, on TPN through L femoral 
venous catheter, chronic poorly controlled abdominal pain, and 
multiple line infections (usually CoNS but most recently 
enterococcus) who presented with fever to 100.1 and chills, 
diffuse body aches, and erythematous line site, was treated with 
Vancomycin until the line was replaced by ___.
. 
# Low-grade fever: It was documented at home, but pt was 
afebrile throughout the hospital stay. There were several 
possible sources of infection included line, pneumonia, urinary 
tract infections, bacteremia.  Pt was started on Vanc 
empirically.  It was decided that line infection was most likely 
especially because some purulent discharge was noted from the 
existing femoral line on presentation.  The IV access team 
recommended an MRV to assess pt's vasculature, however, there 
was concern whether it would be safe since the pt has had a 
dorsal column stimulator placed in her back in ___ for chronic 
pain.  After much investigation, it was discovered that MRI is 
not recommended with the particular device that was implanted in 
her.  Therefore, pt did not have an MRV.  The current left 
femoral line was taken out and another femoral line on the right 
was placed by Interventional Radiology.  All blood cultures were 
negative.  The catheter tip culture of the removed line was sent 
for culture, which was pending at time of discharge.  Vanc was 
discontinued on day of discharge.
.
# Nutrition: A regular diet as tolerated by patient.  Pt's TPN 
was on hold during the hospital stay due to concern for infected 
line.
.
# Chronic DVTs: She has a history of line-associated DVTs.  Pt 
was continued on home lovenox.
.
# Anemia: Hct was trended daily, which remained stable.  Pt was 
continued on home iron.
.
# Depression: Pt was continued on home psych regimen.  Pt was 
maintained on home trazodone prn, aripiprazole, lamotrigine.  
Psych was consulted to aid in our management of this pt who 
recommended frequent communication between the team and pt.
. 
# Pain: Pt was continued on home regimen of amitriptyline, 
gabapentin, clonidine.  Also, pt was continued on a dilaudid PCA 
for additional pain control during hospital stay, with 
understanding that it will be suspended on discharge.
. 
# Sjogrens: Pt was continued on pilocarpine.
. 
# GI dysmotility: Pt was continued on home regimen rabeprazole, 
octreotide, misoprostol.
. 
# Pruritis: Pt was continued on benadryl.
. 
# Hypothyroidism: Pt was continued on levothyroxine.
. 
# Nausea: Pt was given IV phenergan as needed. 
.

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with fever.  Please evaluate for
pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  The lungs are clear.  Persistent elevation of the right
hemidiaphragm is unchanged.  Spinal stimulators are once again visualized. 
There are no pleural effusions.  There are no focal consolidations or
opacities worrisome for pneumonia.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette and hilar
contours are unremarkable.

HISTORY:  A ___ woman with suspected line infection.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ (attending)
performed the procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
Dilaudid PCA and Versed throughout the total intraservice time of 30 minutes,
during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored.
1 mg of Versed and 0.25 mg of Dilaudid were administered.

PROCEDURE:  Written informed consent was obtained from the patient after
explaining the risks, benefits and alternatives and the procedure to the
patient.  The patient was brought to the angio suite and laid supine on the
angio table.  Both the right and left groin were prepped and draped in a
sterile fashion.

Under ultrasound guidance, the right patent common femoral vein was accessed
with a micropuncture needle.  The 0.018 guidewire was inserted through the
needle and was imaged in the IVC via fluoroscopy.  Skin ___ was given and the
needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath.  Then, the inner dilator and
0.018 guidewire was exchanged for a ___.  The ___ was extended into the
IVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  After appropriate measurements were
performed with the tunnel, attention was directed to the right thigh.

Interdermal 1% lidocaine was given at the tunnel entrance site.  Then, a skin
___ was made with a scalpel and 1% lidocaine with epinephrine was injected in
the planned tunnel area.  Then, a tunnel was created using a tunneling device.
Once the catheter was out at the venotomy site, the micropuncture sheath was
exchanged for a #8 ___ dilator.  Once the tract was dilated with an
___ dilator, a ___ peel-away sheath was inserted.  Then, the
dilator and guidewire were removed and the catheter was fed into the IVC.  The
venotomy site was sutured with ___ Vicryl and the catheter was secured with 0
silk.  A StatLock was also applied to the line.  Sterile dressing was applied.

Sterile dressing was taken out from the left femoral catheter.  There was a
small amount of pus that was expressing from the tunnel.  The cuff of the
catheter was outside the tunnel.  The tunnel line was removed and pressure was
held for five minutes over the venotomy site.  There was no hemorrhage from
the line site.  Sterile dressing was applied

The patient tolerated the procedure well and did not have any immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Previous CTA and venogram findings showed central SVC stenosis and a
decision was taken to place a right femoral tunneled line.

2. Left femoral tunneled line removed and tip sent for culture.

3.  Uncomplicated insertion of the right common femoral double-lumen line.
